items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are mostly clear (updateAfterSalePreview, handleImportFromTextarea, getAlreadyRefundedQtyMap). Business-logic lambdas use single letters, e.g. `o => o.id === activeAfterSaleOrderId` and `o.discounts.map(d => ...)`. The 3600-line file has few comments on the money logic.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new 3664-line file, so capped at accept. updateAfterSalePreview re-implements the proportional refund and 'isAll' remaining-payable logic instead of calling the shared refund function. It does at least route actions through shopTestAPI.requestAfterSale and importData.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Hidden test test_cart_rejects_out_of_stock_and_over_stock failed, so stock or quantity guards have gaps. The UI reads quantities with loose `Number(inp.value)` without integer checks. Import failure leaves data unchanged and shows feedback. Some magic constants (low-stock thresholds, 10%).

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: The after-sale modal shows original total, paid amount, amount already refunded, remaining refundable, the formula, and a live preview. But submitAfterSaleFromModal and handleImportFromTextarea run with no confirm step, so refund and import overwrite have no danger confirmation.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls shopTestAPI (requestAfterSale, importData, exportData), so business logic is shared. Money is float with round2, e.g. `round2((origSum * order.payable) / order.subtotal)`, not integer cents. The refund preview duplicates the allocation logic.
